nodes.name: Onboard AI-Driven Autonomous Tasking for Rapid Wildfire Response with a LEO Wide-Swath Observation Satellite
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) remote sensing satellites exhibit significant limitations in emergency response operations, primarily due to the constraints of orbital mechanics and a traditional reliance on ground-involved, open-loop operational models. Current response latencies often span several hours, rendering acquired data less effective for disasters with rapid temporal dynamics. We propose a new intra-pass autonomous reaction application mode to solve this key problem in emergency response. We build the mode on an agile satellite platform operating in an 800 km sun-synchronous orbit. We equip the platform with two core sensors through an innovative design. The two sensors are an optical camera with 0.5-meter resolution and a forward-looking infrared camera. The infrared camera has a 600-kilometer swath and a 10-meter nadir resolution. We take onboard artificial intelligence technologies as the research core. The technologies support real-time and autonomous analysis of forward-looking infrared image data. This analytical capability facilitates the real-time detection and autonomous confirmation of stochastic events, such as wildfires, by leveraging onboard artificial intelligence (AI) to perform real-time analysis of IR imagery. This subsequently triggers immediate autonomous re-tasking for high-resolution follow-up observation within the same orbital pass. We establish an optimization model for the satellite system. The model is used to solve the key balance problem between the sensor forward-looking angle, achievable reaction time, and actual detection resolution. We conduct a detailed engineering time budget analysis for the whole satellite operation system. Analysis results show that a specific forward-looking angle must be set for the infrared camera to obtain a 70-second autonomous response window of the satellite. The 70second window contains 30 seconds for AI cognitive analysis, a maximum of 33.6 seconds for platform attitude maneuvering, and 10 seconds for platform stability adjustment. The minimum forward-looking angle required for the infrared camera is about 33.6 degrees. The ground sampling distance of the infrared camera will decrease to 12.2 meters at this angle. The resulting 12.2-meter ground sampling distance (GSD) remains sufficient to meet the practical requirements of early-stage detection. The proposed Intra-Pass Autonomous Reaction (IPAR) mode reduces emergency response times from hours to seconds, significantly enhancing the proactive observation capabilities of LEO platforms.

nodes.name: Nanosecond pulsed laser coloring technology based on deep learning
nodes.venue: Twenty-First National Conference on Laser Technology and Optoelectronics
nodes.abstract: Nanosecond laser coloring offers significant advantages in corrosion resistance, abrasion resistance, and environmental friendliness. However, accurate prediction and control of coloration effects remain challenging due to the complex, nonlinearly coupled processing parameters. Herein, we propose a deep learning-based framework for both forward and reverse modeling of laser coloration on stainless steel. A dataset comprising 1620 parameter-color pairs was established using a home-built nanosecond laser system. A forward fully connected neural network was trained to map laser parameters to color values, achieving a prediction accuracy above 0.95; notably, the predicted colors exhibit excellent visual and quantitative agreement with the experimental actual colors. For color-driven parameter retrieval, a reverse neural network was constructed. Although the processing parameters predicted by the reverse network deviate substantially from the actual experimental values, feeding these predicted parameters back into the forward model yields a color prediction accuracy of approximately 0.98. This demonstrates that the reverse model can effectively approximate the equivalent solution space of the laser coloring process. Additionally, two self-developed image processing algorithms were specially self-developed for automatic shape correction and rapid color extraction. This work establishes a viable and robust technical pathway for intelligent, customized laser coloration.

nodes.name: Twenty-First National Conference on Laser Technology and Optoelectronics
Integrating Dual-Stream Coordinate and Cross-Spatial Attention for Drone-View Traffic Detection
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract:
Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are essential for traffic monitoring in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). However, the detection of traffic objects in drone-view imagery still faces serious challenges due to drastic scale variations, dense small objects, and complex background clutter. Existing detectors often struggle to effectively separate targets from background noise and lack efficient cross-scale feature interaction mechanisms. This paper introduces ED-DETR, a refined real-time Detection Transformer specifically designed to optimize performance in UAV scenarios.
Specifically, a Dual-Stream Coordinate Attention (DCA) module is designed, which can effectively extract significant texture features while preserving context information through parallel maximum pooling and average pooling operations. In addition, this paper introduces an efficient multi-scale attention structure in the feature fusion neck, which combines grouping convolution and cross-spatial learning to significantly improve the positioning ability of small targets. A large number of experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset show that ED-DETR achieves an mAP of 40.4%, which is significantly higher than that achieved by RT-DETR and other state-of-the-art detectors. By harmonizing high detection accuracy with low computational overhead, the proposed framework enables effective real-time monitoring of aerial traffic scenarios.

nodes.name: Distinguishing artificial intelligence from robotic execution in total knee arthroplasty: a narrative review and evidence map
nodes.venue: Arthroplasty
nodes.abstract: Abstract Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning methods are increasingly discussed in relation to robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, robotic assistance, computer navigation, and AI-based prediction represent distinct functions that are often conflated under the single label “AI-assisted robotic TKA,” obscuring the state of evidence for each. This review clarifies these distinctions and maps the current evidence for AI-related functions across the TKA pathway, keeping AI prediction evidence analytically separate from robotic execution evidence at the level of each clinical function. Methods We performed a critical narrative review and evidence map of peer-reviewed literature relevant to robotic-assisted TKA, navigation-assisted TKA, AI/ML prediction models, digital planning, implant sizing, intraoperative decision support, postoperative monitoring, implementation, and economic evaluation. Evidence was interpreted according to clinical function, comparator structure, validation status, and translational maturity. Because the available literature is methodologically and conceptually heterogeneous, quantitative pooling and formal comparative-effectiveness claims were not attempted. Results Robotic-assisted and navigation-assisted TKA have the most mature evidence base for improving technical precision, particularly implant positioning and radiographic alignment. In contrast, AI/ML evidence is concentrated mainly in adjacent pathway functions, including radiographic interpretation, implant-sizing prediction, patient-selection support, dissatisfaction prediction, outcome modelling, perioperative risk stratification, and postoperative monitoring. Direct clinical evidence demonstrating that AI-enabled robotic TKA provides incremental patient-level benefit beyond conventional robotic assistance remains limited. Current studies are constrained by inconsistent terminology, short follow-up, limited external validation, incomplete reporting of AI components, heterogeneous outcomes, cost uncertainty, and uncertain generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings. Conclusion AI should not currently be treated as a single validated surgical intervention in TKA. Rather, it represents a family of emerging pathway-level functions that may support preoperative planning, intraoperative decision support, patient selection, risk communication, and longitudinal recovery monitoring. Future studies should explicitly define the AI component being evaluated, distinguish AI functionality from robotic or navigation assistance, use standardized comparators, and assess long-term patient-reported outcomes, implant survivorship, safety, cost-effectiveness, and equity across multicenter prospective cohorts or randomized trials.

nodes.name: A Method for Disordered Circlip Recognition Based on Improved YOLOv11 and Association Strategy
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: To realize automated grasping of randomly placed C-type circlips in automotive and mechanical assembly processes, this paper proposes an identification method based on the improved YOLOv11 algorithm and an exclusive association strategy. First, a detail enhancement convolution (DEConv) module is introduced into the C3k2 module of the YOLOv11 network to enhance the ability to capture the edges and high-frequency details of the circlips; Second, the parallel patch-aware attention (PPA) module is adopted in the detection head instead of the traditional convolution, and through multi-branch fusion and channel-spatial attention mechanism, it adaptively focuses on the key areas of small targets; Finally, the normalized Wasserstein distance (NWD) loss function is used instead of the IoU loss to alleviate the gradient disappearance problem in the positioning of small targets and improve the model’s detection accuracy. Based on precise detection, this paper innovatively proposes a circlip-hole association strategy based on multi-level spatial constraints, achieving accurate pairing of randomly placed circlips through bounding box-inclusive attribution judgment, distance screening, and selection of the best circlip-pair. Experimental results show that compared with the original YOLOv11 model, our model improves the mAP50 and mAP50-95 significantly by 5.7% and 3.3%, respectively; its association accuracy reaches above 95%, and the average processing time is 142 ms. Both in terms of accuracy and speed, our model meets the requirements of industrial real-time grasping and provides reliable prior information for the subsequent precise clamping of the robotic arm.

nodes.name: Underwater crack detection with YOLO11s-VFN: a lightweight neck redesign for improved localization
nodes.venue: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
nodes.abstract: Underwater crack detection is challenging due to color cast, low contrast, and complex backgrounds. To improve detection quality while reducing computational redundancy, this paper proposes YOLO11s-VFN (VoVGSCSP Fusion Neck), a lightweight variant of YOLO11s that redesigns the neck for more efficient multi-scale feature fusion. Specifically, the original neck fusion blocks are replaced with VoVGSCSP modules built upon GSConv/GSBottleneck, and the stride-2 downsampling convolutions are substituted by GSConv, aiming to reduce FLOPs while preserving discriminative representations for slender crack patterns. Experimental results on the public Underwater Crack Detection dataset show that, compared with the YOLO11s baseline, YOLO11s-VFN achieves 0.9704 precision and improves mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.8127 to 0.8345, while keeping mAP@0.5 nearly unchanged (0.9552 vs. 0.9558). Moreover, the proposed model reduces computation from 21.3 to 19.7 GFLOPs with slightly fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight neck redesign can enhance localization performance for underwater crack detection and is promising for practical underwater inspection scenarios.

nodes.name: International Conference on Algorithms, Image Processing, and Deep Learning (AIPDL 2026)
Toward AI-Native Integrated Sensing and Communication for 6G Networks
nodes.venue: Journal of Machine Learning Advances
nodes.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is widely regarded as a key enabling technology for sixth-generation (6G) networks. By reusing spectrum, hardware, waveforms, and computing resources, ISAC can provide environmental awareness to support emerging applications such as autonomous transportation, industrial automation, and intelligent Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. However, conventional model-driven ISAC designs are increasingly challenged by dynamic propagation environments, heterogeneous sensing data, high-dimensional joint optimization, and stringent real-time requirements. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI), with its powerful capabilities in learning, reasoning, and prediction, is expected to play a pivotal role in the future evolution of ISAC. Nevertheless, most existing AI-enabled ISAC models are developed for isolated tasks and deployed with limited cross-module coordination, multimodal knowledge sharing, and operational feedback. To address these limitations, this article introduces AI-native ISAC as a system-level architectural paradigm for future 6G networks. The proposed framework consists of five interconnected layers, namely the physical, representation, learning, decision, and feedback layers, which jointly support multimodal environmental representation, continual model evolution, task-oriented decision-making, and closed-loop adaptation. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges associated with the evolution from AI-assisted ISAC to AI-native ISAC, thereby providing a roadmap for future research and development.

nodes.name: SoK: The Security-Safety Continuum of Multimodal Foundation Models
nodes.abstract: Multimodal foundation models (MFMs) integrate diverse data modalities to support complex and wide-ranging tasks. However, this integration also introduces distinct safety and security challenges. In this paper, we unify the concepts of safety and security in the context of MFMs by identifying critical threats that arise from both model behavior and system-level interactions. We propose a taxonomy grounded in information theory, evaluating risks through the concepts of channel capacity, signal, noise, and bandwidth. This perspective provides a principled way to analyze how information flows through MFMs and how vulnerabilities can emerge across modalities. Building on this foundation, we introduce a deterministic minimax formulation to analyze defense mechanisms and to study a structural asymmetry of defense in multimodal systems. Our analysis indicates that model-centric defenses, which primarily operate by suppressing noise or enhancing signal, tend to exhibit diminishing effectiveness against increasingly adaptive attacks. In contrast, system-level safeguards that constrain authorized information flow and agent behavior impose stronger limits on adversarial impact by reducing effective bandwidth. To operationalize this insight, our framework maps attacks and defenses onto information-theoretic axes, effectively organizing and reducing the defense search space. Using a proposed Defense Coverage Index (DCI) to evaluate 15 representative defenses, we observe that system-level bandwidth constraints provide stronger and more consistent protection across attack classes than brittle model-level mechanisms. Finally, we formalize an MFM ``self-destruction threshold'' that specifies when termination should be triggered, offering a concrete activation rule for circuit-breaker safeguards in multimodal systems.

nodes.name: Satellite Image-Based Flooded Road Detection Using Semantic Segmentation
nodes.venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
nodes.abstract: During floods, submerged roads cut off rescue teams from affected people, yet most satellite flood products map general inundation and do not say which roads can still be used. This work presents a deep learning pipeline that identifies accessible routes during floods from satellite imagery. A U-Net with an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 encoder takes co-registered pre-event and post-event four-band tiles from the SpaceNet 8 Germany subset and predicts a road map and a flooded-road map directly. Training combines weighted binary cross-entropy with Dice loss to counter severe class imbalance, and tiles are split into training, validation and test sets by geographic block to avoid spatial leakage. The predicted road mask is skeletonised into a road graph, edges with submerged stretches are removed, and a shortest-path search returns the fastest remaining route between two locations, or reports that none exists. On the held-out test set the model reaches a flooded-road F1 score of 0.74 and a road F1 score of 0.79. In 1,000 sampled origin–destination queries, 93% of the returned routes avoid every truly flooded segment, a route is found for 95% of reachable destinations, and the mean detour is 9% longer than the ideal flood-aware route. Using pre-event imagery and a Dice term raises the flooded-road F1 score from 0.42 to 0.74 over a post-event, cross-entropy baseline. The results show that flood-aware routing from satellite imagery alone is practical for emergency planning.

nodes.name: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering Hub (IRJAEH)
Reconstruction-Aware Observation Selection for Bandwidth-Constrained Multi-UAV Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction
nodes.venue: Drones
nodes.abstract: Multi-UAV observation improves the efficiency and coverage of three-dimensional scene acquisition, but continuous onboard Gaussian Splatting reconstruction is computationally expensive, whereas transmitting dense RGB-D streams wastes communication bandwidth. We propose RAOS-GS (Reconstruction-Aware Observation Selection for Gaussian Splatting), an air–ground collaborative framework for bandwidth-constrained multi-UAV reconstruction. Each UAV maintains a lightweight Gaussian proxy solely to estimate the reconstruction value of candidate observations. The proposed Rendering-Aware Keyframe Selection (RAKS) evaluates uncovered scene content, appearance discrepancy within reliably rendered regions, and relative viewpoint change to retain complementary, non-redundant RGB-D keyframes. The ground station then constructs per-UAV Gaussian submaps, aligns their coordinate frames through cross-UAV RGB-D registration, and jointly refines camera poses and Gaussian parameters to produce a global representation. Experiments on three Replica scenes, two OpenFly-UE virtual outdoor scenes, and three real-world multi-UAV scenes demonstrate a favorable trade-off between observation volume and reconstruction quality. RAOS-GS retains only 5.1%–7.9% of the input observations on Replica and the real-world sequences and 18.7%–24.0% on OpenFly-UE. It consistently outperforms 10% uniform temporal sampling and remains competitive with or surpasses 30% sampling despite using fewer observations. Ablation studies confirm that rendering-aware selection identifies reconstruction-relevant observations, viewpoint constraints suppress redundancy, and ground-side pose–Gaussian refinement improves final reconstruction quality. These results show that reconstruction-aware observation selection can reduce air–ground data transmission without requiring high-fidelity onboard Gaussian mapping.

nodes.name: Quantifying the human visual exposome with vision language models
nodes.venue: Communications AI & Computing
nodes.abstract: Abstract The visual environment is a fundamental yet unquantified determinant of mental health. While the concept of the environmental exposome is well-established, current methods rely on coarse geospatial proxies or biased self-reports, failing to capture the first-person visual context of daily life. Here we show that coupling ecological momentary assessment with vision-language models can quantify the semantic richness of human visual experience. Across 2,674 participant-generated photographs, model-derived estimates of “greenness” robustly predicted momentary affect and chronic stress, consistent with established benchmarks. We then developed a semi-autonomous large language model-based pipeline that mined over seven million scientific publications to extract nearly 1,000 environmental features empirically linked to mental health. When applied to real-world imagery, up to 33% of model-extracted context ratings significantly correlated with affect and stress.

nodes.name: Parents’ experiences of remote parent-mediated communication therapy for toddlers with autism: a qualitative study using Proctor’s implementation outcomes framework
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Parent-mediated interventions, in which therapists guide caregivers to support their child’s communication, are widely used in early autism care, and telehealth may improve access to them. Delivering therapy by videoconference, however, also moves part of the therapeutic work into the home, and families’ experience of this format soon after diagnosis remains poorly understood. This study explored parents’ experiences of remotely delivered Paediatric Autism Communication Therapy, focusing on acceptability, feasibility, appropriateness and fit with family life. Methods This qualitative study was nested in a multicentre randomised controlled trial in France. Fourteen parents of toddlers with autism who had completed the 12-month videoconference programme took part in semi-structured videoconference interviews, conducted within three months of completion by a researcher independent of the intervention. Data were analysed using thematic analysis informed by phenomenological principles, and themes were then mapped onto Proctor’s implementation outcomes framework. Results Four themes were identified: limited alignment with the wider needs of the early post-diagnostic period; positive effects on parental skills, confidence and interactions; influence on family dynamics and routines; and the experience of remote delivery. Parents valued the accessibility of the format, the therapeutic alliance and video feedback, and reported continuing to use strategies after the programme ended. Acceptability was high, whereas appropriateness and feasibility were more variable, shaped by emotional readiness after diagnosis, unaddressed behavioural difficulties, the mental load of recording home videos, and technical problems. Conclusions Remote delivery of this parent-mediated intervention was perceived as acceptable and implementable, mainly through parental empowerment, but it partly shifted the burden of therapy onto households. Preparatory psychoeducation, explicit discussion of the programme’s scope, technical support and hybrid formats may improve its fit with families’ needs early after diagnosis. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04244721. Date of registration: January 28, 2020

nodes.name: Multimodal Collaborative Water-Level Recognition for Water Gauge Images via Improved YOLO26 and Qwen3
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Automatic water-level recognition from water gauge images is fundamentally hindered by limited adaptability to dynamic environments and the susceptibility of E-shaped characters to false detection in complex scenes. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multimodal collaborative framework that integrates VT-BM3D denoising, an improved YOLO26 detector, and Qwen3-VL-driven semantic reasoning for robust water-level recognition. The VT-BM3D algorithm was employed to suppress water-surface reflections and background noise while preserving the edge features of scale markings. The YOLO26 baseline was improved with the CBAM attention mechanism and a P2 small-object detection head. Two recognition modes were then established: the YOLO two-stage mode and the YOLO-Qwen3 joint mode. Experimental results demonstrated that the improved YOLO26 achieved an mAP50 of 86.1% and an mAP50:95 of 67.4% in the second-stage detection of E-characters and the waterline, surpassing the baseline by 8.6 and 8.5 percentage points, respectively. In the evaluated field scenarios, both modes delivered absolute errors below 2 cm, maintaining reading stability and strong anti-interference capability under water-surface reflections, tilted views, and complex backgrounds. These results collectively validate the accuracy, robustness, and practical applicability of the proposed framework for water-level recognition.

nodes.name: Machine learning-based cloud recognition from all-sky camera data for WFST observation optimization
nodes.venue: Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics
nodes.abstract: Abstract To support cloud-aware observations with the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST), we built a region-level dataset from 400 nighttime all-sky images acquired at the Lenghu site between October 2023 and September 2024. The dataset covered 123 nonconsecutive observing nights and comprised 12,800 region-level samples. The valid sky area in each image was divided into 32 regions, each assigned one of three labels: "cloud-free," "partially obscured," or "fully obscured." Frozen Vision Transformer (ViT) encoders from the DINO (self-distillation with no labels) family were shared across regions for feature extraction, while a separate classifier was trained for each of the four radial levels. Four handcrafted feature sets served as baselines, and 95 representation-classifier configurations were compared using five-fold cross-validation grouped by observation night. The combination of DINOv2 ViT-S/14 class-token features and a support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel (RBF SVM) performed best, with five-fold mean values of 91.69%, 91.48%, and 0.8757 for balanced accuracy, macro-averaged F1 score, and the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), respectively. Its balanced accuracy was 7.12 percentage points higher than that of the best handcrafted feature configuration and exceeded 90% in all three lunar-illumination groups (bright, gray, and dark nights). Compared with handcrafted features, this configuration achieved higher overall classification performance and smaller performance differences across the four radial levels. The regional predictions can be mapped back to their original spatial positions to produce a spatial cloud-cover map that can serve as region-level input for WFST dynamic scheduling and cloud-aware observations.

nodes.name: Lightweight YOLOv8n marigold corolla detection and picking-point localization method based on ECR progressive channel compression and dual attention mechanisms
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Plant Science
nodes.abstract: To address insufficient detection accuracy and picking-point positioning difficulties from dense occlusion of marigold corollas in fields, we propose a lightweight detection and spatial localization method. A Femto Mega depth camera acquires top-view color and depth images. For detection, we adopt YOLOv8n, introduce AIFI (Attention-based Intra-scale Feature Interaction) to replace SPPF for enhancing global context, employ C2fAttn (C2f with Attention) dynamic feature weighting in neck to replace C2f for strengthening local detail on dense overlaps, and propose ECR (Efficient Channel Reduction) progressive compression for lightweighting via attention-compensated channel loss. For localization, we propose a picking-point positioning algorithm using depth and spherical fitting, with centroid offset correction and sphere intersection for 3D coordinates. Experiments show model parameters 1.2M (60% compression) and mAP@0.5 98.7%; average localization errors 4.5 mm indoors and 7.5 mm outdoors, with system error 2–18 mm. When corolla stem inclination exceeds 30°, the top-view spherical fitting fails, which is the main constraint in unstructured fields. At tilt angles not exceeding 30°, the positioning accuracy met the tolerance requirements of the end-effector of the harvesting manipulator, and the theoretical picking point was consistently located below the actual harvestable position. These results indicate that the proposed method maintains high accuracy while substantially reducing model complexity, thereby providing a feasible solution for intelligent harvesting of marigolds.

nodes.name: Lamb wave damage localization method for carbon fiber-reinforced polymer plates based on 1DCNN-KAN and physics-informed data augmentation
nodes.venue: Engineering Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Lamb wave-based structural health monitoring (SHM) technology provides an effective means for online damage monitoring of carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) plates. However, affected by the complex multimodal and dispersive characteristics of Lamb waves, feature extraction from damage monitoring signals heavily relies on manual experience. To address this issue, this paper proposes an automatic Lamb wave damage localization method integrated with deep learning, where an end-to-end deep learning framework fusing the one-dimensional convolutional neural network and the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (1DCNN-KAN) is developed. Taking raw damage monitoring signals as input, the 1D-CNN is adopted to extract local features of the signals, while the KAN decision layer explicitly models the mapping relationship between features and damage locations through learnable one-dimensional spline functions, thereby realizing structural damage localization without complex manual signal feature extraction. For damage location prediction, the damage monitoring area is gridded, and random damage is mapped to different grid nodes to achieve classification-based damage localization. To tackle the difficulty in acquiring monitoring signals of damage at arbitrary locations, a physics-informed data augmentation method is proposed, which generates Lamb wave monitoring signals covering random damage locations across the entire monitoring area based on the signals acquired at grid nodes. Finally, damage localization experiments are carried out on a CFRP plate. For damage of different sizes at 40 random locations (the minimum damage size is 10 mm × 5 mm × 20 mm), the 1DCNN-KAN model achieves grid-cell-level positioning for all test samples, and the predicted damage location and the actual location are both within the same grid cell (with a grid cell resolution of 20 mm × 20 mm). The classification accuracy of the damage location reaches 100%. Comparisons with different models demonstrate the superior performance of 1DCNN-KAN. This study provides an intelligent solution for damage localization of CFRP plates.

nodes.name: INSIGHT-X: Multimodal VLM Assistant for Artifact Localization, and Mitigation Guidance in X-ray Inspection
nodes.venue: IMAPSource Proceedings
nodes.abstract: Advanced semiconductor packages rely on X-ray CT and laminography for non-destructive inspection of buried interconnects and internal structures. However, dense metal features and heterogeneous materials often introduce artifacts, including ring artifacts, beam-hardening streaks, geometric distortions, and missing-cone artifacts. These artifacts obscure critical features during inspection, reduce reconstruction fidelity, and complicate defect interpretation, requiring expert-driven and iterative troubleshooting. To address these challenges, we propose INSIGHT-X, a vision–language model framework for artifact diagnosis, localization, root-cause and mitigation in X-ray inspection workflows. INSIGHT-X formulates artifact analysis as a multimodal question-answering task by integrating reconstructed X-ray images, artifact annotations, and expert knowledge into an artifact-centric dataset. Through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, the model learns to identify artifact types, localize affected regions, and generate interpretable explanations. The system also provides artifact-aware cause and mitigation recommendations, including general acquisition and reconstruction adjustments, and calibration guidance. By combining visual understanding, spatial localization with explainable answers, INSIGHT-X transforms expert knowledge into a scalable AI assistant for improving inspection consistency, accelerating troubleshooting, and supporting decision-making in advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

nodes.name: Feasibility of Workstation-Level BLE Localization for Classroom Attendance: A Multi-Granularity Evaluation of Kalman-Filtered and Relational RSSI Features
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Credential-based attendance mechanisms such as QR codes and RFID cards record who checked in but not whether that person is physically present, which makes them vulnerable to proxy attendance. Vision-based alternatives depend on line of sight and camera coverage, whereas Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) indoor positioning can passively verify the presence of a student’s device. However, received signal strength indicator (RSSI) measurements are highly sensitive to multipath propagation, so neighboring workstations with similar signal characteristics are difficult to distinguish. This study evaluates the feasibility of workstation-level BLE localization in a classroom with 40 workstations and four beacons. RSSI was smoothed with a Kalman filter and combined with relational features, namely beacon ranks and pairwise RSSI differences, as inputs to Weighted K-Nearest Neighbor (WKNN), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers at 40, 20, 8, and 4 location classes. Kalman filtering improved accuracy for all four models at every granularity (+3.34 to +11.89 percentage points); for the two main models, WKNN and RF, all paired cluster-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of this gain were above zero (+4.58 to +8.71 percentage points). The relational features improved tree-based ensembles at 40 classes (RF: +1.38 percentage points, 95% CI [+0.03, +2.88]; XGBoost: +1.35 percentage points, point estimate) but reduced WKNN accuracy at the finer granularities. RF reached 40.68% accuracy at 40 classes, 61.06% at 8 classes, and 73.37% at 4 classes, and all four classifiers performed similarly at 40 classes. These results show a clear trade-off between spatial resolution and classification reliability with four beacons; identity binding and session-level attendance decisions remain to be evaluated.

nodes.name: Edge-Deployed AI Safety Compliance System with Real-Time Multi-Class PPE Detection, Face Recognition, and Automated Physical Access Control
nodes.venue: Pakistan Journal of Engineering and Technology
nodes.abstract: Manual monitoring of personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance in industrial workplaces is labor-intensive, subject to supervision by humans and presents challenges for continuous safety enforcement. In this work, we propose a single embedded platform to integrate real-time multi-class personal protective equipment detection, worker identification, temporal compliance verification, and automated physical access control for an edge-deployed AI safety compliance system. It is based on Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (8 GB RAM) and does not need continuous cloud computing or external GPUs. YOLOv11-nano detector optimized with NCNN framework is used for the PPE detection in 12 classes, while YuNet-FaceNet pipeline implemented via ONNX Runtime is used for the worker identification based on face. The physical access-control interface is implemented with a GPIO-controlled relay, and the stability of compliance decisions before granting access is increased with a five-state finite state machine with a 15-frame majority-voting scheme. The detection model was trained on a combined dataset of >6,000 images of 12 PPE classes, including a subset collected specifically for earmuff and headset detection. The system achieved 0.843 mAP@0.5, 0.841 F1-score on the held-out test set, and field-tested response times of 312-321 ms, well below the 500 ms operational goal. The system can reach 2.3% false-alarm rate and 90% detection at 3 m under normal operating conditions. For adverse lighting, the performance drops to mAP@0.5 of 0.693. The results demonstrate that multi-class PPE detection, worker identification, temporal decision making, event logging and physical access control can be integrated on low-cost embedded hardware without the need for continuous internet connectivity or dedicated server infrastructure.

Comparing Multisource Optical Satellite Imagery Products for River Discharge Estimation using Deep Learning
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing of river discharge (RSQ) has advanced rapidly with increasing satellite availability and the development of data-driven methods capable of generating predictions directly from images. Here, we retrain and evaluate the transferability of a recently developed transformer-based deep learning (DL) model with five medium resolution multispectral products using 2,760 gauges distributed globally. The model captures discharge-relevant signal directly from variations in reflectance. We further evaluated the impacts of sensor harmonization, atmospheric correction, and differences in revisit frequency. Performance was broadly consistent across products with median correlation and Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) values ranging from 0.55 to 0.59 and -0.03 to 0.04, respectively. Differences between best and worst performing products per site generally varied moderately without exhibiting clear geographic patterns. Performance was largely insensitive to dominant land cover classes and dam presence but declined in correlation for rivers wider than 250 m. Gauge-calibrated, model-calibrated, and uncalibrated iterations of C/M approaches provide different baseline comparisons with respect to predictive skill and usage cases. Site-level scaling errors resulting in bias remains a primary limitation of the DL model. These findings demonstrate discharge-relevant information for image-based RSQ is transferable across optical sensors and processing levels, supporting flexible discharge monitoring globally using multisource satellite imagery.

nodes.name: An Intelligent Computer Vision Framework for Duplicate Part Detection in Complex CAD Assemblies
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract:
Duplicate components in large-scale Digital Mock-Up (DMU) assemblies present a significant challenge to product integrity within Digital Twin environments operating on integrated OEM Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) platforms. These duplicates, often referred to as structural redundancies or doubloons, are characterized by geometrically identical or equivalent components occupying the same spatial location without corresponding justification in the Bill of Materials (BOM). Such inconsistencies arise from increasing assembly complexity, tool integration issues, and limitations of conventional scripting-based validation approaches.
Existing duplicate detection methods rely heavily on manual inspection and isolated tool functionalities, making them impractical for large-scale assemblies. While interference analysis tools can detect spatial conflicts, they cannot reliably distinguish between valid engineering overlaps and unintended duplicate conditions. Consequently, a more structured and automated validation strategy is required.
This paper presents an automated computer vision-based methodology developed within an OEM Digital Twin environment to address these challenges. The proposed framework combines interference-data extraction, image-based overlap assessment, automated duplicate screening, Active Feedback Learning, and BOM-integrated validation within a unified workflow. The methodology transforms interference-derived information into structured analytical features and uses Red Percentage–based overlap evaluation to identify potential duplicate conditions.
The proposed approach enables scalable duplicate detection across complex assemblies while reducing dependence on manual review. Validation on production-scale automotive DMU datasets demonstrated significant reductions in engineering effort and substantial filtering of non-actionable interference records. By integrating computer vision analytics, feedback-driven noise elimination, and product structure validation, the proposed framework improves Digital Twin data integrity and supports efficient engineering workflows in modern OEM PLM environments.

nodes.name: A Digital Twin Framework Integrating Multiscale Signal Decomposition and Hybrid Deep Learning for Intelligent Water Storage Control on Remote Islands
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Precipitation on remote offshore islands is characterized by non-stationarity and strong stochasticity. However, rainwater harvesting systems require accurate precipitation forecasts to ensure effective water storage and discharge and a stable freshwater supply. Here, we propose an intelligent framework integrating precipitation signal decomposition, a hybrid neural network for predicting daily precipitation over the next 30 days, and digital twin technology to optimize water storage and discharge strategies for rainwater collection pools. For signal preprocessing, variational mode decomposition decomposes the original daily precipitation series into multiple intrinsic mode functions, a chaotic sparrow search optimization algorithm performs global parameter optimization, and singular spectrum analysis is applied twice to denoise high-frequency mode components. The hybrid prediction model combines a convolutional neural network to extract local temporal features, bidirectional long short-term memory to capture bidirectional long-term dependencies, and a multilayer perceptron for nonlinear mapping and regression output. Finally, this model is integrated into a digital-twin-enabled decision framework to automatically implement water storage control through water balance calculations and threshold comparisons. The proposed method achieves a test mean absolute error of 2.49 mm, a root mean square error of 5.72 mm, and an R2 of 0.83; digital twin control significantly reduces overflow losses and, during typical typhoon months, maintains the water level in the rainwater collection pool below the warning threshold. In summary, we present a simulation-based pathway for optimizing small-scale intelligent rainwater harvesting systems, which offers a practical pathway to enhance the sustainability of freshwater resources on remote offshore islands by improving the efficiency of rainwater utilization and reducing dependence on external water supplies.
